{{Short description|American chemist (1939–2023)}}
'''William Carl Lineberger''' (December 5, 1939 – October 17, 2023) was an American chemist.

==Life and career==
A native of [[Hamlet, North Carolina]], William Carl Lineberger was born to parents Caleb Henry and Evelyn Pelot Cooper Lineberger on December 5, 1939. His mother was a former teacher and his father was a railroad worker. Through his mother, Lineberger is of [[French Huguenot]] descent. As a child, Lineberger was a [[Boy Scouts of America|Boy Scout]] and made [[Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle]] rank.<ref name="autobio">{{cite journal |last1=Lineberger |first1=W. Carl |title=Autobiography of W. Carl Lineberger |journal=J. Phys. Chem. A |date=January 21, 2010 |volume=114 |issue=3 |pages=1227–1229 |doi=10.1021/jp911450m |pmid=20088610 |url=https://jila.colorado.edu/faculty/w-carl-lineberger|bibcode=2010JPCA..114.1227L |url-access=subscription }}</ref> After completing his bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], Lineberger began teaching at his alma mater, leaving for a research position at the [[Ballistic Research Laboratory|U. S. Army Ballistic Research Laboratory]] and later the [[Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics]]. The [[University of Colorado at Boulder]], one of two joint operators of JILA, hired Lineberger as an assistant professor in 1970. He was named E. U. Condon Distinguished Professor of Chemistry at the University of Colorado in 1985.<ref name="wclcv">{{cite news |title=Lineberger, William Carl |url=https://experts.colorado.edu/display/fisid_101695 |accessdate=December 17, 2018 |publisher=University of Colorado}}</ref>

Over the course of his career, Lineberger received several awards. Among them are: the [[Herbert P. Broida Prize]] (1981) awarded by the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy]] (1992), [[Irving Langmuir Award]] (1996) and [[Peter Debye Award]] (2004) of the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref name="wcljournalcv">{{cite journal |last1=Lineberger |first1=W. Carl |title=Curriculum Vita of W. Carl Lineberger |journal=J. Phys. Chem. A |date=January 28, 2010 |volume=114 |issue=3 |pages=1231–1232 |doi=10.1021/jp911447z|bibcode=2010JPCA..114.1231. |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the [[William F. Meggers Award in Spectroscopy]] (1989) from the [[Optical Society of America]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=OSA Awards Mark Achievements in Many Facets of Optical Science |journal=Physics Today |date=July 1, 1989 |volume=42 |issue=7 |page=85 |doi=10.1063/1.2811098|bibcode=1989PhT....42g..85. }}</ref> Lineberger received the [[NAS Award in Chemical Sciences]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carl Lineberger Wins NAS Award in Chemical Sciences |url=https://jila.colorado.edu/news/carl-lineberger-wins-nas-award-chemical |accessdate=December 17, 2018 |publisher=JILA |date=January 22, 2015}}</ref> Lineberger was a member of the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref name="wclcv"/><ref name="wcljournalcv"/> as well as the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (1983)<ref>{{cite news |title=W. Carl Lineberger |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/w-carl-lineberger-vaidlr/ |access-date=December 17, 2018 |publisher=United States National Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1995).<ref name="wclcv"/><ref name="wcljournalcv"/> He was a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref name="wclcv"/><ref name="wcljournalcv"/> and the [[American Physical Society]] (1973).<ref>{{cite news |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=L |accessdate=December 17, 2018 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> From 2011 to 2016, Lineberger served on the [[National Science Board]] and was nominated for a second term by [[Barack Obama]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |title=Senate Confirms Fellow Carl Lineberger as Member of the National Science Board |url=https://jila.colorado.edu/news/senate-confirms-fellow-carl-lineberger-member-national-science-board |accessdate=December 17, 2018 |publisher=JILA |date=August 5, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Fostering Integrity in Research |date=2018 |publisher=National Academies Press |isbn=9780309391252 |page=231 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XxVEDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA231}}</ref>

Lineberger died on October 17, 2023, at the age of 83.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remembering JILA Fellow W. Carl Lineberger {{!}} JILA - Exploring the Frontiers of Physics |url=https://jila.colorado.edu/news-events/news/remembering-jila-fellow-w-carl-lineberger |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=jila.colorado.edu}}</ref>
